history.summary: Freehold 1BR at Kensington Square, D19 (Bartley), 760m from CC12 Bartley MRT, asking $978k at $1,356 PSF for an efficient 721 sqft. Reasonable 46-txn URA base supports a credible (if modest) 4.87%/yr rate; PSF sits ~20% under the $1,707 median.
history.rating_rationale: Solid fundamentals but unexciting: freehold, MRT-connected, mixed-use convenience, and an honest 46-txn appreciation series — but at only 4.87%/yr, below the RCR/OCR-blend you'd want. $978k for a 1BR is at the upper end for the bed count, and the catalyst story (Bartley is mature, no major new govt zone) is thin. A safe hold, not a growth play.
red_flags: $978k is high for a 1BR — narrows resale to investors
catalysts: Efficient 721 sqft layout, broad rental appeal

history.summary: Freehold mixed-use 1BR near Bartley/Serangoon MRT, asking $1,356 psf sits at/below the verified recent transaction range, making the algo's cheapness real but tempered by a thin 141-unit liquidity profile.
history.rating_rationale: Asking $1,356 psf ($978k, 721 sqft FH) is at the very bottom of the verified last-12-month range of $1,360-$1,773 psf (avg ~$1,656 over 49 sales) per EdgeProp/PropertyGuru — so the -23.2% age-adj cheapness is corroborated by real transactions, not a quirk. Freehold tenure plus the 2030 Cross Island Line build-out around Hougang/Serangoon adds a dated catalyst. Confidence held to medium because psf_cohort_txns is only 5 and the 141-unit mixed-use development is small, so resale liquidity at exit is thinner than the large mass-market peers; trailing appreciation (4.87%) is discounted per the backtest prior.
red_flags: Small 141-unit mixed-use development implies thinner resale liquidity at exit
psf_cohort_txns only 5 - cheapness signal rests on a modest comparable set
Mixed-use (commercial podium) can mean noise/footfall and a narrower buyer pool
catalysts: Cross Island Line stations around Hougang/Serangoon North targeted 2030
Freehold tenure in a leasehold-heavy district
